claim: Insulin promotes glucose uptake into fat and muscle cells to lower postprandial blood glucose downstream of Akt activation.
source: Insulin, downstream of Akt activation, promotes glucose uptake into fat and muscle cells to lower postprandial blood glucose, an enforced change in cellular metabolism to maintain glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known biological function of insulin.

claim: Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in fat and muscle cells is mediated by the Glut4 glucose transporter.
source: This effect is mediated by the Glut4 glucose transporter.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Growth factors enhance glucose uptake to fuel anabolic metabolism required for tissue growth and repair, predominantly mediated by Glut1.
source: Growth factors also enhance glucose uptake to fuel an anabolic metabolism required for tissue growth and repair. This activity is predominantly mediated by the Glut1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Akt is activated by phosphorylation of its kinase domain and hydrophobic motif (HM) domains.
source: Akt is activated by phosphorylation of its kinase and hydrophobic motif (HM) domains.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Insulin-stimulated Glut4-mediated glucose uptake requires PDPK1 phosphorylation of the kinase domain (T309) but not mTORC2 phosphorylation of the HM domain (S474).
source: We show that insulin-stimulated Glut4-mediated glucose uptake requires PDPK1 phosphorylation of the kinase domain but not mTORC2 phosphorylation of the HM domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: An intact HM domain is required for Glut4-mediated glucose uptake despite S474 phosphorylation not being required.
source: Nonetheless, an intact HM domain is required for Glut4-mediated glucose uptake.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by domain deletion experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Glut1-mediated glucose uptake requires both PDPK1 phosphorylation of T309 and mTORC2 phosphorylation of S474.
source: Whereas, Glut1-mediated glucose uptake also requires mTORC2 phosphorylation of the HM domain, demonstrating both phosphorylation-dependent and independent roles of the HM domain in regulating glucose uptake.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: mTORC2 links Akt to distinct physiologic programs related to Glut4 and Glut1-mediated glucose uptake.
source: Thus, mTORC2 links Akt to the distinct physiologic programs related to Glut4 and Glut1-mediated glucose uptake.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the differential requirement for mTORC2 phosphorylation.

claim: Akt family kinases have regulatory roles in numerous physiologic processes including cell growth, proliferation, differentiation, metabolism, cell migration and survival.
source: The Akt family of kinases are a major node in cell signaling, with regulatory roles in numerous physiologic processes, including cell growth, proliferation, differentiation, metabolism, cell migration and survival (Manning and Cantley, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Perturbations in Akt signaling are linked to diseases including hyper-activation in cancer and blunted activity in metabolic diseases.
source: Perturbations in Akt signaling are linked to many diseases, from hyper-activation in cancer to blunted activity in metabolic diseases (Franke, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: There are three Akt homologues: Akt1, Akt2 and Akt3 (also referred to as protein kinase B (PKB)α, -β and -γ, respectively).
source: There are three Akt homologues: Akt1, Akt2 and Akt3 (also referred to as protein kinase B (PKB)α, -β and -γ, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: All three Akt isoforms share a common domain structure consisting of an amino-terminal pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, a kinase domain, and a carboxyl-terminal regulatory region referred to as the hydrophobic motif (HM) domain.
source: All three share a common domain structure consisting of an amino-terminal pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, a kinase domain, and a carboxyl-terminal regulatory region referred to as the hydrophobic motif (HM) domain (Chan et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Canonical Akt activation involves plasma membrane recruitment to sites of PI3K activity by Akt PH domain binding to PIP3.
source: The canonical mode of Akt activation involves plasma membrane recruitment to sites of phosphoinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) activity by Akt PH domain binding to phosphoinositide 3,4,5 trisphosphate (PIP3), the product of growth factor activation of PI3K (Vivanco and Sawyers, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Akt is phosphorylated in its kinase domain at T308/9 by PDPK1 concurrent with plasma membrane recruitment.
source: Concurrent with plasma membrane recruitment, Akt is phosphorylated in its kinase domain at T308/9 (residue number for Akt1 and Akt2, respectively) by phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDPK1), which is itself recruited to the plasma membrane by its own PH domain (Frech et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Full Akt activation is associated with a second phosphorylation on S473/4 in the HM domain by mTORC2.
source: Full Akt activation is associated with a second phosphorylation on S473/4 in the HM domain by mTORC2 (Sarbassov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The exact link between growth factor stimulation and activation of mTORC2 activity is not known.
source: The exact link between growth factor stimulation and activation of mTORC2 activity is not known (Sparks and Guertin, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: T308/9 phosphorylation is key for Akt activation.
source: The kinase domain phosphorylation, T308/9, is key for activation (Alessi et al., 1996)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: S473/4 phosphorylation of the HM domain allosterically enhances kinase activity and contributes to substrate selectivity.
source: whereas S473/4 phosphorylation of the HM domain allosterically enhances kinase activity (Alessi et al., 1997) and contributes to substrate selectivity (Jacinto et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Akt transmits insulin signaling to control cellular metabolism.
source: A major function of Akt is to transmit insulin signaling to the control of cellular metabolism.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Akt plays a role in insulin-stimulated translocation of Glut4 glucose transporter to the plasma membrane of fat and muscle cells.
source: One well characterized biological output of Akt is its role in insulin-stimulated translocation of Glut4 glucose transporter to the plasma membrane of fat and muscle cells (Jiang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The redistribution of Glut4 underlies enhanced glucose uptake responsible for postprandial blood glucose lowering.
source: The redistribution of Glut4 underlies enhanced glucose uptake responsible for postprandial blood glucose lowering (Abel et al., 2001; Zisman et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Akt mediates growth factor stimulated glucose uptake into cells other than fat and muscle.
source: Akt also mediates growth factor stimulated glucose uptake into cells other than fat and muscle (Ward and Thompson, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Enhanced Glut1-mediated glucose uptake by cancer cells is a prominent example of growth factor-stimulated glucose uptake untethered from regulation of whole body glucose homeostasis.
source: Enhanced Glut1-mediated glucose uptake by cancer cells is a prominent example of growth factor-stimulated glucose uptake untethered from regulation of whole body glucose homeostasis (Carvalho et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Technical impediments have made it challenging to define Akt isoform-specific roles and the precise roles of the two activating phosphorylations in signal transduction.
source: However, technical impediments have made it challenging to define Akt isoform-specific roles as well as the precise roles of the two activating phosphorylations in signal transduction.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a motivation for the study.

claim: The authors developed a system to study ectopically expressed Akt without interference from endogenous Akt using MK2206-resistant Akt2-W80A.
source: We developed a system to study ectopically expressed Akt without interference from endogenous Akt (Kajno et al., 2015). The ectopically expressed Akt is engineered to contain a mutation in the PH domain (W80A) that confers resistance to MK2206, an allosteric Akt inhibitor (Calleja et al., 2009; Green et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Acute inhibition of endogenous Akts with MK2206 allows for functional studies of the ectopically expressed Akt, while minimizing compensatory changes due to loss of Akt functions.
source: Acute inhibition of endogenous Akt's with MK2206 allows for functional studies of the ectopically expressed Akt, while minimizing compensatory changes due to loss of Akt functions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a methodological advantage.

claim: The authors previously used the Akt2-W80A system to study Akt isoform specificity in adipogenesis.
source: We have previously used this system to study Akt isoform specificity in adipogenesis (Kajno et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Phosphorylation of T309 by PDPK1 is required for Glut4 translocation.
source: Phosphorylation of T309 by PDPK1 is required for Glut4 translocation, whereas phosphorylation of S474 by mTORC2 is not required.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding of the study and supported by data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Insulin-stimulated Glut1 translocation to the plasma membrane of adipocytes and proliferative cells is dependent on both T309 and S474 phosphorylations.
source: However, insulin-stimulated Glut1 translocation to the plasma membrane of adipocytes and proliferative cells is dependent on both T309 and S474 phosphorylations, linking growth factor regulation of Glut1-mediated glucose uptake to mTORC2 activity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding of the study and supported by data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: HA-Glut4-GFP expression in transfected adipocytes showed about 1.5 fold increase in total Glut4 staining compared to untransfected cells.
source: The cells expressing HA-Glut4-GFP showed about 1.5 fold increase in total Glut4 staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells expressing Akt2-W80A showed about two fold increase in total Akt compared to untransfected cells.
source: while cells expressing Akt2-W80A showed about two fold increase in total Akt (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ectopically expressed constructs (HA-Glut4-GFP and Akt2-W80A) are expressed to about the same level as native proteins.
source: These data demonstrate that the constructs are expressed to about the same level as native proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the quantification data from Figure 1 supplements.

claim: A 30 min incubation with 1 nM insulin promoted an approximate 10-fold increase of Glut4 in the plasma membrane of control adipocytes.
source: A 30 min incubation with 1 nM insulin promoted an approximate 10-fold increase of Glut4 in the plasma membrane of control adipocytes, and co-expression of Akt2-W80A did not affect insulin response (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Co-expression of Akt2-W80A did not affect insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation response.
source: A 30 min incubation with 1 nM insulin promoted an approximate 10-fold increase of Glut4 in the plasma membrane of control adipocytes, and co-expression of Akt2-W80A did not affect insulin response (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A 60 min pre-incubation with 1 µM MK2206 abolished insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in control adipocytes.
source: A 60 min pre-incubation with 1 µM MK2206 abolished insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in control adipocytes, whereas Glut4 translocation was unaffected by MK2206 in cells expressing Akt2-W80A (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Glut4 translocation was unaffected by MK2206 in cells expressing Akt2-W80A.
source: A 60 min pre-incubation with 1 µM MK2206 abolished insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in control adipocytes, whereas Glut4 translocation was unaffected by MK2206 in cells expressing Akt2-W80A (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of Akt2-W80A fully rescued Akt phosphorylation of FoxO1 in cells in which native Akts are inhibited by MK2206.
source: Expression of Akt2-W80A fully rescued Akt phosphorylation of FoxO1 and partially rescued Akt T642 phosphorylation in cells in which native Akts are inhibited by MK2206 (Figure 1D,E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Expression of Akt2-W80A partially rescued AS160 T642 phosphorylation in cells in which native Akts are inhibited by MK2206.
source: Expression of Akt2-W80A fully rescued Akt phosphorylation of FoxO1 and partially rescued Akt T642 phosphorylation in cells in which native Akts are inhibited by MK2206 (Figure 1D,E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: AS160 phosphorylation is not linearly correlated with Akt regulation of Glut4 translocation.
source: The Akt2-W80A partial rescue of AS160 phosphorylation, in context of its complete rescue of Glut4 translocation (Figure 1C), indicates that AS160 phosphorylation is not linearly correlated with Akt regulation of Glut4 translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the comparison of AS160 phosphorylation and Glut4 translocation data.

claim: MK2206 inhibited insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in control adipocytes in a dose-dependent manner, with an EC50 of less than 0.1 µM.
source: MK2206 in a dose-dependent manner, inhibited insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in control adipocytes, with an EC50 of less than 0.1 µM MK2206 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Adipocytes co-expressing Akt2-W80A were resistant to up to 1 µM MK2206.
source: Adipocytes co-expressing Akt2-W80A were resistant to a dose up to 1 µM MK2206.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 1 µM MK2206 can be used to distinguish ectopically expressed Akt2-W80A activity from the activities of endogenous Akts.
source: Thus, 1 µM MK2206 can be used to distinguish ectopically expressed Akt2-W80A activity from the activities of endogenous Akt's.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the dose-response data.

claim: The insulin dose-response of Glut4 translocation in MK2206-treated adipocytes expressing Akt2-W80A was similar to that in untreated control adipocytes.
source: The insulin dose-response of Glut4 translocation in MK2206-treated adipocytes expressing Akt2-W80A, was similar to that in untreated control adipocytes, validating this as an experimental system to quantitatively assess Akt function downstream of insulin stimulation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Glut4 translocation was fully blocked by 1 µM MK2206, but AS160 phosphorylation on T642 was only partially inhibited.
source: Although Glut4 translocation was fully blocked by 1 µM MK2206, AS160 phosphorylation on T642 was only partially inhibited (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Akt phosphorylation of AS160-T642 is not a linear readout of Akt control of Glut4 translocation.
source: Thus, Akt phosphorylation of AS160-T642 is not a linear readout of Akt control of Glut4 translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the discrepancy between AS160 phosphorylation and Glut4 translocation.

claim: Insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation on T309 and S474, and phosphorylation of AS160 on T642 were unaffected by 1 µM MK2206 in adipocytes expressing Akt2-W80A.
source: Insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation on T309 and S474, and phosphorylation of AS160 on T642 were unaffected by 1 µM MK2206 in adipocytes expressing Akt2-W80A, in agreement with the results of Glut4 translocation (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: MK2206 did not affect the insulin dose-response of Akt2-W80A phosphorylation on T309 and S474.
source: As was the case for the insulin-dose response measured by Glut4 translocation, MK2206 did not affect the insulin dose-response of Akt2-W80A phosphorylation on T309 and S474, confirming the system can be used to quantitatively assess Akt activation downstream of insulin-stimulation (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Mutation of both T309 and S474 blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation.
source: Mutation of both T309 and S474 blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation, as did the single mutation of T309, demonstrating that T309 phosphorylation is necessary for Akt2 to signal to Glut4 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Single mutation of T309 blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation, demonstrating that T309 phosphorylation is necessary for Akt2 to signal to Glut4.
source: Mutation of both T309 and S474 blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation, as did the single mutation of T309, demonstrating that T309 phosphorylation is necessary for Akt2 to signal to Glut4 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Glut4 translocation was fully supported by Akt2-W80A-S474A mutant, establishing that S474 phosphorylation is not required for insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation.
source: Surprisingly, Glut4 translocation was fully supported by Akt2-W80A-S474A mutant, establishing that S474 phosphorylation is not required for insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Akt2-T309A and Akt2-S474A mutants were expressed to similar levels.
source: Akt2-T309A and Akt2-S474A mutants were expressed to similar levels, demonstrating that the functional difference between these mutants was not due to difference in the expression levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by expression data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474 was unaffected by T309A mutation, demonstrating T309 phosphorylation is not a prerequisite for S474 phosphorylation.
source: Insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474 was unaffected by T309A mutation, demonstrating T309 phosphorylation is not a prerequisite for S474 phosphorylation (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The S474A mutation did not affect T309 phosphorylation.
source: Similarly, the S474A mutation did not affect T309 phosphorylation (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: In adipocytes, T309 and S474 phosphorylations are independent of one another.
source: Thus, in adipocytes these phosphorylations are independent of one another.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the phosphorylation data from mutants.

claim: Akt2-W80A-S474A supported insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S6 kinase, an mTORC1 target downstream of Akt.
source: Akt2-W80A-S474A supported insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S6 kinase, an mTORC1 target downstream of Akt (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Akt activation of mTORC1 does not require phosphorylation of S474.
source: Thus, in addition to Glut4 translocation, Akt activation of mTORC1 does not require phosphorylation of S474.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the S6 kinase phosphorylation data.

claim: The T309A mutation blunted insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S6 kinase, consistent with phosphorylation of T309 being required for Akt activity.
source: As expected, the T309A mutation blunted insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S6 kinase, consistent with phosphorylation of T309 being required for Akt activity (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation promoted by endogenous Akt was unaffected in adipocytes expressing either T309A or S474A mutants compared to control adipocytes.
source: Insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation promoted by endogenous Akt (cells not treated with MK2206) was unaffected in adipocytes expressing either T309A or S474A mutants compared to control adipocytes (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The T309A and S474A mutants are not dominant-interfering of endogenous Akt.
source: These data establish that the mutants are not dominant-interfering of endogenous Akt.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the data showing no effect on endogenous Akt function.

claim: PDPK1 is responsible for phosphorylation of T309, and mTORC2 for phosphorylation of S474.
source: PDPK1 is responsible for phosphorylation of T309, and mTORC2 for phosphorylation of S474 (Sarbassov et al., 2005; Alessi et al., 1997; Jacinto et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Transient knockdown of mTORC2 activity by targeting the Rictor subunit had no effect on Glut4 translocation, despite reducing insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474 by approximately 80%.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, transient knockdown of mTORC2 activity by targeting the Rictor subunit had no effect on Glut4 translocation, despite reducing insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474 by approximately 80% (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A-D.

claim: mTORC2 knockdown did not affect phosphorylation of T309.
source: As expected, mTORC2 knockdown did not affect phosphorylation of T309.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4C-D.

claim: The PDPK1 inhibitor, GSK2334470, blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The PDPK1 inhibitor, GSK2334470, blocked insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The inhibition of Glut4 translocation by GSK2334470 correlated with reduced T309 phosphorylation.
source: The inhibition of translocation correlated with reduced T309 phosphorylation (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: GSK2334470 did not affect insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474.
source: GSK2334470 did not affect insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of S474.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4F.

claim: S474 phosphorylation is dispensable, whereas T309 phosphorylation is essential for Glut4 translocation in adipocytes.
source: These results reinforce the conclusion that S474 phosphorylation is dispensable, whereas T309 phosphorylation is essential for Glut4 translocation in adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the combined data from PDPK1 inhibition and Rictor knockdown.

claim: Substitution of aspartate for S474 (S474D) generates a constitutively active Akt, presumably as a phosphomimetic.
source: Several studies have demonstrated that substitution of aspartate for S474 (S474D) generates a constitutively active Akt, presumably as a phosphomimetic (Yang et al., 2002a, 2002b; Hart and Vogt, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Akt2-W80A-S474D promoted Glut4 translocation in the absence of insulin stimulation.
source: In agreement with that previous work, Akt2-W80A-S474D promoted Glut4 translocation in the absence of insulin stimulation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: T309 was constitutively phosphorylated in the S474D mutant without insulin stimulation.
source: Consistent with the functional activity, T309 was constitutively phosphorylated in the S474D mutant; that is, without insulin stimulation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Akt2-W80A-S474D-induced Glut4 translocation was blocked by T309A mutation.
source: The Akt2-W80A-S474D-induced Glut4 translocation was blocked by T309A mutation as well as by PDPK1 inhibition (Figure 5A and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A and D.

claim: The Akt2-W80A-S474D-induced Glut4 translocation was blocked by PDPK1 inhibition.
source: The Akt2-W80A-S474D-induced Glut4 translocation was blocked by T309A mutation as well as by PDPK1 inhibition (Figure 5A and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A and D.

claim: The aspartate substitution at S474 alters Akt2 in a way that enhances phosphorylation of T309 by basal activity of PDPK1, resulting in Akt2 activation and Glut4 translocation, yet phosphorylation of S474 is not required for Glut4 translocation.
source: Thus, the aspartate substitution at S474 alters Akt2 in a way that enhances phosphorylation of T309 by basal activity of PDPK1, resulting in Akt2 activation and Glut4 translocation, yet phosphorylation of S474 is not required for Glut4 translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the S474D mutant data.

claim: A naturally occurring mutation in the Akt PH domain, E17K, enhances association with the plasma membrane, independent of stimulated PI3 kinase activity, leading to constitutive Akt activity and Glut4 translocation in adipocytes.
source: A naturally occurring mutation in the Akt PH domain, E17K, enhances association with the plasma membrane, independent of stimulated PI3 kinase activity, leading to constitutive Akt activity and Glut4 translocation in adipocytes (Gonzalez and McGraw, 2009b; Carpten et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A was blocked by the T309A mutation.
source: Increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A was blocked by the T309A mutation as well as by the PDPK1 inhibitor GSK2334470, providing independent evidence that Glut4 translocation is dependent on PDPK1 phosphorylation of T309 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A was blocked by the PDPK1 inhibitor GSK2334470.
source: Increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A was blocked by the T309A mutation as well as by the PDPK1 inhibitor GSK2334470, providing independent evidence that Glut4 translocation is dependent on PDPK1 phosphorylation of T309 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The S474A mutation had no effect on the increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A, consistent with Glut4 translocation being independent of S474 phosphorylation.
source: The S474A mutation had no effect on the increased plasma membrane Glut4 induced by expression of Akt2-E17K-W80A, consistent with Glut4 translocation being independent of S474 phosphorylation (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: S474 phosphorylation has been linked to target selection.
source: S474 phosphorylation has been linked to target selection (Jacinto et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: Akt2 in which the HM domain was deleted (Akt2-kinase domain construct) did not support insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation, despite the deletion construct being expressed to the same level as full length Akt2-W80A.
source: Akt2 in which the HM domain was deleted (Akt2-kinase domain construct) did not support insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation, despite the deletion construct being expressed to the same level as full length Akt2-W80A (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: T309 in Akt2-kinase domain construct was phosphorylated in insulin-stimulated cells, demonstrating the HM domain is not required for PDPK1 to phosphorylate Akt2 T309.
source: T309 in Akt2-kinase domain construct was phosphorylated in insulin-stimulated cells, demonstrating the HM domain is not required for PDPK1 to phosphorylate Akt2 T309 but the HM domain is required for Glut4 translocation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The HM domain is required for Glut4 translocation.
source: T309 in Akt2-kinase domain construct was phosphorylated in insulin-stimulated cells, demonstrating the HM domain is not required for PDPK1 to phosphorylate Akt2 T309 but the HM domain is required for Glut4 translocation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the domain deletion data.

claim: Akt in which the PH domain was deleted (kinase-HM domains) did not support Glut4 translocation, confirming that plasma membrane targeting is required.
source: In addition, Akt in which the PH domain was deleted (kinase-HM domains) did not support Glut4 translocation, confirming that plasma membrane targeting is required (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The HM domain provided in trans did not rescue Glut4 translocation in cells expressing Akt2-kinase domain construct.
source: The HM domain provided in trans did not rescue Glut4 translocation in cells expressing Akt2-kinase domain construct (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Co-expression of the HM domain with a PH domain fused to its amino terminus (PH-HM domain) rescued insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation activity to the Akt2-kinase domain construct.
source: However, co-expression of the HM domain with a PH domain fused to its amino terminus (PH-HM domain), rescued insulin-stimulated Glut4 translocation activity to the Akt2-kinase domain construct (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Expression of the PH-HM domain alone had no effect on Glut4 translocation.
source: Expression of the PH-HM domain alone had no effect on Glut4 translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The enhanced co-localization of the Akt2 kinase domain and the HM domain achieved when both are independently targeted to plasma membrane sites of PI3 kinase activity was required for complementation of the HM domain in trans.
source: Thus, the enhanced co-localization of the Akt2 kinase domain and the HM domain achieved when both are independently targeted to plasma membrane sites of PI3 kinase activity was required for complementation of the HM domain in trans.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the complementation data.

claim: S474 of the PH-HM domain construct was not phosphorylated in insulin-stimulated adipocytes, providing further support that S474 phosphorylation is not required for Glut4 translocation.
source: Despite this functional complementation, S474 of the PH-HM domain construct was not phosphorylated in insulin-stimulated adipocytes, providing further support that S474 phosphorylation is not required for Glut4 translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the Western blot data in Figure 6C.

claim: Both stably expressed Akt2-W80A and Akt2-W80A-S474A support translocation of HA-Glut4-GFP reporter.
source: We established that both stably expressed Akt2-W80A and Akt2-W80A-S474A support translocation of HA-Glut4-GFP reporter.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in Akt2-W80A-S474A adipocytes was only 70% of that in cells expressing Akt2-W80A, despite Akt2-W80A-S474A supporting full translocation of Glut4 to the plasma membrane.
source: Unexpectedly, insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in Akt2-W80A-S474A adipocytes was only 70% of that in cells expressing Akt2-W80A, despite Akt2-W80A-S474A supporting full translocation of Glut4 to the plasma membrane (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 7A and B.
